claim: The Production front 'I'd like to go' is exactly what Lesson 17's いきたいです answers, and nothing on the front asks for the softened request-opener form instead.
evidence: Production front: 'Travel & Tourism / I'd like to go' (no hint). Ledger, chapter-17: 'いきたいです | (I) want to go'; chapter-16: 'ええ、ぜひいきたいです | Yes, I'd love to go'. The extras card paul-want-to-go-tokyo-dome solves the same problem with the hint 'Asking a station employee for directions'.
fix: Add a hint such as 'opening a request for directions, leaving the question unsaid' so the front asks for いきたいんですが rather than いきたいです.
verdictReason: Checked. Production front is only "Travel & Tourism / I'd like to go" with no hint or scene; the ledger has いきたいです "(I) want to go" (chapter-17) and ええ、ぜひいきたいです "Yes, I'd love to go" (chapter-16). The book glosses the word "I'd like to go", so the English is faithful, but card-rules-shared.md says when one English shape maps to two structures the hint names the structure. paul-want-to-go-tokyo-dome already does this with a scene; the headword card does not.

claim: The Production front fits both か and にち, and the card's own note says both are used for counting days.
evidence: Production front: '…days (counter) / after a number, counting days'. Back note: 'Also 〜にち, depending on the number.' The same unit's ichinichi card counts one day as いちにち, and Lesson 7 taught 'にち | Day (suffix)'. Nothing on the front says which numbers are meant.
fix: Say on the front which numbers it covers (for example 'counting two to ten days, the native reading'), so にち is ruled out.
verdictReason: Checked. The front ("…days (counter) / after a number, counting days") fits にち as well as か: the ledger has にち "Day (suffix)" (chapter-7) and the same unit ships ichinichi, which counts a day with にち. The card's own note says "Also 〜にち, depending on the number" and the futsuka note states the rule ("two to ten days use か"), so the information to disambiguate exists on the back but not the front. The book lists the headword as 〜か／にち; the deck carded か alone (にち was dedup-excluded), so the front has to say which numbers.

claim: GRAMMAR 3 contrasts かかります (a time felt as long) with "period です" (a time not felt as long); the card gives only the first half and no card in either unit teaches the second.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "The verb かかります means 'take time' and is used when the speaker considers the time to be long. When the speaker does not feel the time to be long, 'period です' is used." Card kakarimasu-2 note: "Used when the speaker feels the time is long. Regular 1." No note or sentence in chapter-20 or chapter-20-extras uses or mentions the period です alternative.
fix: Extend the kakarimasu-2 note with the book's other half (when the time does not feel long, say the period + です instead, e.g. 10ぷんです), keeping the "feels the time is long" clause, which the book states. Optionally add an extras sentence of that shape from taught words.
verdictReason: Merged with the Learner's note-unverifiable finding on the same note. The Learner's claim that the book does not make this statement is wrong: GRAMMAR 3 says かかります "is used when the speaker considers the time to be long", and the book's own example is 40 minutes, so the 15/30-minute extras do not contradict it and the clause must not be dropped. What is true in both findings is that the note gives half of the book's contrast: GRAMMAR 3 continues "When the speaker does not feel the time to be long, period です is used", and a grep of both units for ぷんです/じかんです/かんです/ねんです finds no card or note carrying that half. Without it the note reads as the Learner read it. Fix is the Reader's: extend the note with the period です half (an extras sentence of that shape is optional).

claim: GRAMMAR 3 and 4 both teach that a length of time goes straight before かかります or います with no particle after it, and no card back states this.
evidence: Book, GRAMMAR 3: "The amount of time is placed immediately before the verb かかります and no particle is needed after it." GRAMMAR 4: "The period spent in a certain place is placed immediately before the verb います, with no particle after it." Cards: kakarimasu-2 note "Used when the speaker feels the time is long. Regular 1."; imasu-stay note "With a length of time it means you stay somewhere for that long."; gr4-london-3nen-imashita note "ぐらい after the period makes it approximate". The sentences show the pattern but none explains it.
fix: Add one line to the kakarimasu-2 and imasu-stay notes: the length of time comes right before the verb and takes no particle (さんじかん かかります, いっしゅうかん います).
verdictReason: Checked. GRAMMAR 3 and 4 both state the period goes immediately before かかります / います with no particle. Grepped both units' rendered notes for "no particle", "without a particle", "straight/right/immediately before": nothing. kakarimasu-2, imasu-stay and gr4-london-3nen-imashita notes say nothing about it; the ten かかります sentences and the stay sentences only show it. A rule the book states and no back states is a gap; polish is the right weight because every sentence models it correctly.

claim: やすみのひ needs ひ meaning 'day', but the only ひ the learner has met means 'fire', so they cannot build 'on my days off' this way.
evidence: Target: 'やすみのひは、ねぼうするのがすきです'; Production front: 'On my days off, I like sleeping in.' Ledger: 'ひ | Fire' (chapter-12) is the only ひ card; 'やすみ | Vacation, day off' exists, so a learner says やすみは and is marked wrong. The note explains ねぼうする and のがすきです but not ひ.
fix: Rewrite with taught words (しゅうまつは、ねぼうするのがすきです or やすみは、ねぼうするのがすきです), or keep やすみのひ and add to the note that ひ here means "day" (やすみのひ, a day off), with romaji and gloss as the hint/note rule requires.
verdictReason: Merged: both roles filed the same problem under the same id. Checked the ledger and every cards.json in the collection: the only card with target ひ is chapter-12-extras/fire ("Fire"), and やすみのひ appears in no unit but chapter-20-extras. The note explains ねぼうする and のがすきです but not ひ. Lesson 20 does not print ひ, so the AI-authored sentence (aiSuggested, 2026-10-12 owner request) uses an untaught word in a card the learner has to produce. Either fix works: gloss ひ "day" in the note, or rewrite with a taught time word (しゅうまつは …, or やすみは …, both in the ledger).

claim: 'Sleeping in' is not the gloss the learner was given for ねぼう, so the Production front points as much to ねる as to ねぼうする.
evidence: Production front: 'On my days off, I like sleeping in.' The base cards teach 'ねぼうします | Oversleep' and 'ねぼうする | Oversleep (dictionary form)'; the ledger has 'ねます | Sleep, go to bed'. The link between sleeping in and ねぼう is only in the back note.
fix: Add a hint naming the verb (for example 'use the verb for oversleeping'), or gloss it 'I like oversleeping (sleeping in)'.
verdictReason: The fact is checked: the deck glosses ねぼうします/ねぼうする as "Oversleep" and nothing the learner has seen links "sleeping in" to it, while ねる "Sleep, go to bed" and ねるのが… constructions are in the ledger (chapter-15). Whether a learner reaches for ねるのがすきです instead is a judgement about the front I cannot settle. What settles it: the owner's view on whether the English should track the deck's own gloss ("I like oversleeping") or carry a hint naming the verb. If the untaught-prerequisite fix rewrites the sentence, fold this in at the same time.

claim: The Production front prints the same disambiguator twice, once as the hint and once inside the English, on yokka, futsuka, muika, itsuka and mikka.
evidence: Production front for yokka: 'Time / Four days / a length of time / a length of time, not a date'. The same doubled lines appear on futsuka, muika, itsuka and mikka.
fix: Keep one of the two lines (the fuller 'a length of time, not a date' is enough).
verdictReason: Checked in cards.json and the rendered faces: yokka, futsuka, mikka, itsuka and muika each carry scene "a length of time" AND hint "a length of time, not a date", and the template prints both on the Production front, so the learner sees the disambiguator twice. The scene alone is what keeps the Recognition front apart from the Lesson 7 dates; the hint is the fuller text. Keep one per face (drop the hint, or shorten the scene), and treat the five cards as one fix. ichinichi has only the hint and is fine.

claim: The romaji for ねぼうします is written as one word on the base cards and as two words everywhere else in the chapter.
evidence: neboushimasu: 'Says: nebōshimasu'; nebou-shimashita: 'Says: nebōshimashita'. But nebou-suru-dict-form note: 'nebō shimasu'; extras overslept-no-breakfast: 'nebō shimashita'; neboushimasu-tokidoki: 'nebō shimasu'; nebou-suru-dict-form: 'nebō suru'.
fix: Use one spacing on all ねぼう cards (nebō shimasu / nebō shimashita, matching nebō suru).
verdictReason: Checked every pronunciation in both units: neboushimasu "nebōshimasu" and nebou-shimashita "nebōshimashita" are joined; nebou-suru-dict-form ("nebō suru", and "nebō shimasu" in its note), dlg-nebou-uchi-o-demashita, overslept-no-breakfast, neboushimasu-tokidoki and yasumi-ni-nebou-suru-no-ga-suki all space it. The two headword cards are the odd ones out; the spaced form matches the rest of the chapter. Preflight's romaji lint does not cover this, so it is not already reported.

claim: The note refers to a chart the learner has never seen.
evidence: Note: 'The chart writes it in brackets. Add it when you want to state a period of time clearly, as in ごふんかん.' No card shows a chart.
fix: Drop 'The chart writes it in brackets.' and keep the rest, which already says it is optional.
verdictReason: Checked. The note's "The chart writes it in brackets" refers to the WORD POWER II period chart, which the book prints and no card shows (the learner meets the chart only as 36 separate cards). The sentence is faithful to the book but dangles for a learner without it; the rest of the note already says the suffix is optional and when to add it, so dropping the first sentence loses nothing.

claim: The dictionary and て-form cards carry only 'R1 verb' or 'R2 verb', an abbreviation no earlier card used, while the masu cards in the same unit say 'Regular 1' and 'Regular 2'.
evidence: noru-dict, noru-te, tsuku-dict, tsuite-te, kakaru-dict, kakatte-te note: 'R1 verb'; oriru-dict, orite-te, deru-dict, dete-te note: 'R2 verb'. norimasu-2 note: 'The vehicle takes に. Regular 1.' Earlier notes (chapter-15 かく, たべる) spell out 'Regular 1' / 'Regular 2' and say how the form is made.
fix: Spell it 'Regular 1' / 'Regular 2' and, as Lesson 15's notes did, say how the form comes from the masu form (のります → のる → のって).
verdictReason: Checked. All ten dictionary and て-form cards (noru-dict, noru-te, tsuku-dict, tsuite-te, kakaru-dict, kakatte-te: "R1 verb"; oriru-dict, orite-te, deru-dict, dete-te: "R2 verb") have that two-word note and nothing else. A grep of the ledger with --notes finds no earlier note using "R1"/"R2" and 86 using "Regular 1"/"Regular 2"; norimasu-2 and imasu-stay in this very unit say "Regular 1"/"Regular 2". One caveat for the fixer: the book's vocabulary does mark verbs "(R2)", so the abbreviation is not invented, but card-authoring-rules.md requires the note to name the class and the change (Lesson 15's notes do), and these notes give neither the derivation nor the deck's spelling of the class.
